# Batch 23 reconciliation — resolutions and fix plan (read-only; every figure below is re-derivable by the command beside it)

Baseline facts used throughout: branch DB `user_version` 100; batch session stem `session_2026-10-01-research-batch-23` (S); `origin/main` = 464eb31, copy at `/tmp/claude-0/main.db`. All queries ran `mode=ro`. One permitted check script (`test_verification_pipeline.py`) copies the DB to a `mkstemp` file by its own design; nothing else wrote.

## 1. Resolutions

| # | What I found (evidence) | Disposition | §8 reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | `add-source` requires `--tier` and refuses a tier that contradicts `derive_tier(evidence_type, scope)` (`scripts/db.py` ~3140–3150); the Co-1 refusal tests only that `co1_provenance` is non-empty (`db.py:3182`). `evidence_type`, `tier`, `co1_source_type` have **no CHECK** (`dbcore.check_values` returns `[]` for all three; D-0178 §Notes says the same of tier). F1's contradiction was semantic — same bytes shape as FUB/CERMI, different judgment — so no derivable refusal exists; a bytes-rooted warrant quote (RC1 style) would have *passed* REF-01022 ("netwerk VAN mensen…" is in the artefact). Post-capture: `_AMENDABLE` (`db.py:5103`) excludes `evidence_type`; tier moves only paired with `--field scope` (`db.py:5300–5365`), and `co1` admits only `intrinsic` (`schemas/tier_derivation.py:70`), so a mis-tiered Co-1 row is unfixable after capture except by hand SQL — the "coverage bug" `db.py:5330`'s own comment names. The scratch re-file lost the warrant history: `select co1_provenance from evidence_sources where ref_id='REF-01022'` → NULL. | **BUILD** the correction path (WP-N1); **CUT** the idea of a derivable Co-1 refusal | The wrong thing reaching the book is a ● full-band Co-1/T6 standing on a source that cannot carry it, uncorrectable after capture; the L4 lens caught it, the writer cannot, and a quote-presence gate would not have. |
| I2 | A row carries `created_at` at **minute** precision (`dbcore.now()`, `dbcore.py:190`) and nothing marks completion; ordering vs the search is unknowable from the row. `log_search` refuses an empty prior (`db.py:703`) and cannot know when it was written. Derive: 63 rows created 03:05–03:41 (`select min(created_at),max(created_at) from search_executions where created_by_session=S`) against 31 `WebSearch` tool_use blocks at 02:36–02:5x in `transcripts/harness_5b214a57/main.jsonl`; `backfill=1` on one row (exec 184); disclosure note on 45 rows. The contract already demands the order ("WITH --prior-expectation written BEFORE you run it"); the tooling never supported it, because results are known only after. | **BUILD**, conditional on I5's ledger (WP-N4); if N3 is declined, **NARROW** R8's text to "the row holds a prior; precedence is unenforced" | Only a tool-call timestamp outside the DB can witness precedence; without it a two-phase verb proves nothing but writer-stamp order (a tautology). |
| I3 | R7: `expected = max(1, screened//25)` (`research_batch_dod.py:170,428`). `results_screened = results_found` on 63/63 batch rows and 173/191 corpus-wide (`select sum(results_screened=results_found),count(*) from search_executions`). The floor failed at 5/266 and was met by seven one-hit "web" rows (execs 175–181, found=1/screened=1, logged 03:10) plus candidates 141–147, six `OUT-OF-SCOPE` (`select disposition,count(*) from search_candidates where created_by_session=S group by 1` → 8 of 12); final 12 candidates vs 318 screened = floor exactly. `results_screened` is read by nothing else: no view (`sqlite_master` scan), no other script (`grep -rl results_screened scripts --include=*.py` → dod and db.py). Candidate substance is already bytes-checked by RC1: `provenance_artefact_audit` is blocking, `min_items: 1`, and 12/12 batch candidates carry `surfaced_in`. | **CUT** the floor (WP-N2) | Both terms of the ratio are typed by the party being judged; the real check (candidate rooted in bytes) exists and is blocking, so the floor measures nothing the book depends on. |
| I4 | The gate tests `search_executions.language<>'EN' AND target_evidence_type='grey'` (`dod.py:400`) — a proxy on search *targets*; the contract's claim is about *admitted peer-reviewed work*. It fired on execs 157/171 (a DPO remissvar, a platform methodology — not peer-reviewed) and was cleared by re-targeting them `co1`; 12 non-EN execs now target `co1` (query above, I ran it). No waiver token exists (R1 has `CO1-NOT-APPLICABLE`; R5 none). The three non-EN `grey` admissions today (REF-01022 `letter`, 01025 `grey`, 01029 `report`; `lang_detected` nl/sv/es, no journal, no DOI) are exactly what R5 permits. | **NARROW** (WP-N2) | A non-English journal article filed `grey` drops from ● to ○ in the determination; a DPO letter filed `grey` does not, and forcing it to `co1` corrupts `v_coverage_branch`'s Co-1 count. |
| I5 | `.claude/settings.json` has one `PostToolUse` entry, matcher `Bash` → `record-command.py`, which exits unless `tool_input.command` exists; no WebSearch/WebFetch capture. The transcript holds the tool calls (31 `WebSearch`, 0 `WebFetch` this harness session; reviewer counted 28 at d3d3cd2, 27 logged). The session→transcript mapping is derivable (`commands.jsonl` `session_id` → `transcripts/harness_<sid[:8]>`, `preserve_transcripts.py:128`). The bare `curl` probes **are** already in `commands.jsonl` (5 lines name law.go.kr/nld.go.kr; manifest 2) — the gap is the comparison, not the capture. `research_contract_hook.py --check` reads only `SessionStart[0]` (lines 90, 175), so a PostToolUse edit cannot trip `research_contract_sync`. | **BUILD** (WP-N3) | The wrong thing: a coverage claim ("KR: wrong index / translation not found", feeding `v_coverage_jurisdiction` and R14's "genuine absence") built on a result set never screened; only a reviewer diffing the transcript by hand found it. |
